text: Two environments similar conditions rank genotypes similarly. kernel turns intuition covariance matrix. Linear (GB). environmental analogue VanRaden’s genomic relationship matrix: 𝐊E=𝐖𝐖⊤tr(𝐖𝐖⊤)/q \mathbf{K}_E = \frac{\mathbf{W}\mathbf{W}^{\top}}                     {\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf{W}\mathbf{W}^{\top})/q} trace normalisation puts kernel scale comparable 𝐊G\mathbf{K}_G, variance components two sources can read . Gaussian (GK). Similarity decays nonlinearly distance: k(𝐰i,𝐰j)=exp⁡(−h‖𝐰i−𝐰j‖2q50) k(\mathbf{w}_i, \mathbf{w}_j) = \exp\!\left(-h\,   \frac{\lVert \mathbf{w}_i - \mathbf{w}_j \rVert^2}{q_{50}}\right) q50q_{50} median squared Euclidean distance, making bandwidth scale-free. Use doubling stress double penalty — common heat drought, damage threshold-like. Arc-cosine deep (DK). Emulates infinitely wide neural network deep.layers hidden layers (Cuevas et al. 2019), recursively: k(l)(𝐰i,𝐰j)=1πkii(l−1)kjj(l−1)(sinθ(l−1)+(π−θ(l−1))cosθ(l−1)) k^{(l)}(\mathbf{w}_i,\mathbf{w}_j) = \frac{1}{\pi}   \sqrt{k^{(l-1)}_{ii} k^{(l-1)}_{jj}}   \left(\sin\theta^{(l-1)} + (\pi - \theta^{(l-1)})\cos\theta^{(l-1)}\right) bandwidth tune, cost interpretability. return value two parts. envCov environment × environment — one goes model. varCov covariable × covariable, diagnostic showing covariables move together. Arc-cosine deep kernels emulate deep network without bandwidth parameter: One kernel per developmental stage: kernel performs best empirical. Compare cross-validation, inspection.

title: Envirotyping for Quantitative Genetics and Plant Breeding
text: EnvRtype fits enviromics-enabled reaction-norm models phenotypes regressed genomic, environmental GxE relatedness kernels. current prediction workflow provides: Kernel construction — get_kernel() assembles genomic (K_G), environmental (K_E) soil (K_S) kernels; env_kernel() builds Gaussian / linear environmental kernels; decompose_kernels(), undecompose_kernels() truncate_gxe_kernel() manage GxE block structure. Model fitting — kernel_model() fits multi-kernel Bayesian reaction-norm model; kernel_model_mc() runs multiple chains; kernel_model_clustered() fits environment-clustered models built env_cluster() / cluster_environments(). Validation & variance — kernel_cv() runs cross-validation (CV1 / CV2 / CV0 schemes) varcomp_summary() reports variance components share variance explained kernel. Untested environments — scan_untested_envs() predicts genotype performance environments phenotypes, grid_scan(), map_scan(), scan_spatial_table() coverage_summary() summarise target population environments (TPE). tools implement reaction-norm kernel methods Costa-Neto et al. (2021, G3), nonlinear / Gaussian kernels Costa-Neto, Fritsche-Neto & Crossa (2021, Heredity), deep kernels Cuevas et al. (2019, G3), BGGE GxE engine Granato et al. (2018, G3), envirome-wide prediction untested environments Costa-Neto et al. (2023, G3). title: Build the Matrix of Environmental Covariables for Reaction Norm — W_matrix
text: env.data data.frame environmental variables get_weather, already summarised object .processed = TRUE. .processed boolean. Indicates whether data.frame previously processed summaryWTH already contains means, medians, etc. id.names character. Columns used id environmental variables. env.id character. Column used id environments. var.id vector (character). variables used analysis. probs vector (numeric). Probability quantiles \([0,1]\), used statistic = 'quantile'. NULL, c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75). .interval boolean. Indicates temporal intervals must computed inside environment. Default FALSE. time.window vector (numeric). .interval = TRUE, temporal breaks. names.window vector (character). .interval = TRUE, interval names. center boolean. Indicates whether matrix centred. Default TRUE. scale boolean. TRUE, variables assume \(x \sim N(0,1)\). Default TRUE. sd.tol numeric. Maximum standard deviation tolerated quality control. Default 10. statistic vector (character). Statistic computed, c('','sum','mean','quantile'). Default 'mean'. tol numeric. Numerical tolerance; variables whose standard deviation tol treated near-constant flagged removal. Default 1E-3. QC boolean. Indicates whether Quality Control applied. QC removes variables sd(x) > sd.tol near-constant variables. impute character. handle missing values scaling: "none" (default, keep NAs), "mean" (column mean), "median" (column median), "knn" (k-nearest-environment imputation, see knn) "drop" (remove columns NA). knn integer. Number nearest environments used impute = "knn". missing cell filled mean covariable knn similar environments (Euclidean distance standardised, commonly observed covariables). Default 5. max.cor numeric \((0,1]\) NULL. NULL, greedy collinearity filter (rule caret::findCorrelation) drops covariables pair retained covariables absolute Pearson correlation max.cor. two covariables correlated one larger mean absolute correlation rest removed. Unlike sd-based rules explicit opt-collinear covariables always dropped (independently QC). Default NULL (collinearity filtering). group boolean. used max.cor NULL. TRUE, collinear covariables grouped instead dropped: covariables clustered average-linkage hierarchical clustering \(1 - |r|\), tree cut height \(1 - \)max.cor, correlated block replaced mean (single composite covariable). block--member mapping returned "groups" attribute. Default FALSE (collinear covariables dropped). cor.report NULL, TRUE, character path. NULL, per-covariable collinearity diagnosis (largest absolute correlation, partner responsible, final status, block belongs ) written CSV. Pass TRUE write "W_matrix_collinearity.csv" current working directory, directory write file , full file path. Default NULL (file written). table always attached "collinearity" attribute. verbose boolean. TRUE (default) prints quality-control messages. copula character NULL. NULL, covariable matrix replaced copula-based indices computed env_copula. One "none" (default, NULL), "pobs", "joint", "survival", "kendall" "". See env_copula meaning index. copula.args list. Extra arguments passed env_copula, e.g. list(groups = list(heat = c("T2M_mean","T2M_MAX_mean")), ties.method = "average").

title: Build the Matrix of Environmental Covariables for Reaction Norm — W_matrix
text: Quality control follows Morais Junior et al. (2018): covariables whose standard deviation across environments exceeds sd.tol discarded, near-constant covariables (\(sd \le tol\)) carry information environmental differences. Three , independent cleaning steps available. Missing values can imputed column-wise (impute = "mean"/"median") similar environments (impute = "knn") statistic computed, avoids silently shrinking covariable set way impute = "drop" . Redundant covariables can pruned max.cor: enviromic matrices frequently contain near-duplicated columns (e.g. several temperature summaries), inflate Euclidean geometry relatedness kernels; greedy filter keeps one representative per correlated block. Unlike earlier versions, numerical tolerance added data scaling (silently shifted unscaled outputs); used detect near-constant columns.

code: ## A scan is normally produced by scan_untested_envs(); here we build a ## minimal one by hand -- 3 genotypes across 6 candidate sowing windows -- ## so the example is self-contained. gids <- paste0("G", 1:3) envs <- paste0("sow", 1:6) mu <- matrix(c(6, 5.5, 5), 3, 6) +       matrix(rep(c(0, .4, .7, .6, .2, -.3), each = 3), 3, 6)  # peaks mid-window dimnames(mu) <- list(gids, envs) scan <- list(   yHat_matrix = mu, yHat_lower = mu - 0.5, yHat_upper = mu + 0.5,   interpolation = data.frame(     env               = envs,     position          = c("interpolation", "interpolation", "edge",                           "interpolation", "mild_extrapolation",                           "gross_extrapolation"),     mahalanobis_ratio = c(0.6, 0.8, 1.4, 0.9, 2.1, 3.6),     prop_outside      = c(0, 0, 0.1, 0, 0.3, 0.7),     weight_negativity = 0, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)) class(scan) <- "scan_untested_envs"  ## Map each scanned environment to a calendar sowing date dates <- data.frame(env = envs,                     date = as.Date("2024-04-01") + c(0, 14, 28, 42, 56, 70))  ## Best *supported* sowing date per genotype (gross extrapolations dropped) best_planting_date(scan, dates) #>   gid  best_date yHat lower upper position n_dates_considered #> 1  G1 2024-04-29  6.7   6.2   7.2     edge                  5 #> 2  G2 2024-04-29  6.2   5.7   6.7     edge                  5 #> 3  G3 2024-04-29  5.7   5.2   6.2     edge                  5  ## Rank every date, including the out-of-envelope ones best_planting_date(scan, dates, exclude_flagged = FALSE) #>   gid  best_date yHat lower upper position n_dates_considered #> 1  G1 2024-04-29  6.7   6.2   7.2     edge                  6 #> 2  G2 2024-04-29  6.2   5.7   6.7     edge                  6 #> 3  G3 2024-04-29  5.7   5.2   6.2     edge                  6  ## Stricter: also drop mild extrapolations before ranking best_planting_date(scan, dates, envelope_level = "mild") #>   gid  best_date yHat lower upper position n_dates_considered #> 1  G1 2024-04-29  6.7   6.2   7.2     edge                  4 #> 2  G2 2024-04-29  6.2   5.7   6.7     edge                  4 #> 3  G3 2024-04-29  5.7   5.2   6.2     edge                  4

code: ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 1. Cluster a genetic-correlation matrix directly (no model needed) ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Six environments forming two obvious groups R <- matrix(0.2, 6, 6) R[1:3, 1:3] <- 0.9 R[4:6, 4:6] <- 0.85 diag(R) <- 1 dimnames(R) <- list(paste0("E", 1:6), paste0("E", 1:6))  ## Automatic number of clusters via silhouette width cl <- cluster_environments(R) cl$k #> [1] 4 cl$table #>   env cluster sil_width #> 1  E1       1     0.875 #> 2  E2       1     0.875 #> 3  E3       1     0.875 #> 4  E4       2     1.000 #> 5  E5       3     1.000 #> 6  E6       4     1.000 cl$silhouette["average"] #> average  #>  0.9375   ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 2. Force a specific number of clusters ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ cluster_environments(R, k = 2)$clusters #> E1 E2 E3 E4 E5 E6  #>  1  1  1  2  2  2   ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 3. Try different algorithms and distances ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ cluster_environments(R, k = 2, method = "pam", seed = 1)$medoids #> [1] "E1" "E4" cluster_environments(R, method = "kmeans", k_range = 2:4, seed = 1)$clusters #> E1 E2 E3 E4 E5 E6  #>  3  3  3  1  4  2  cluster_environments(R, distance = "sqrt",                      hclust_linkage = "complete")$clusters #> E1 E2 E3 E4 E5 E6  #>  1  1  1  2  3  4   # \donttest{ ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ ## 4. Full workflow from phenotypes, kernels and a fitted model ## ------------------------------------------------------------------ data("maizeYield"); data("maizeG"); data("maizeWTH")  ECs <- W_matrix(env.data = maizeWTH[maizeWTH$daysFromStart < 100, ],                 var.id = c("FRUE", "PETP", "SRAD", "T2M_MAX")) #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> W_matrix -- builds the environmental covariable (W) matrix #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #>   - summarising weather data into environmental covariables #>   - centring, scaling and quality-controlling W K <- get_kernel(K_G = list(G = maizeG),                 K_E = list(W = env_kernel(env.data = ECs)[[2]]),                 data = maizeYield, model = "RNMM") #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> env_kernel -- builds environmental relatedness kernels #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #>   - computing a single environmental kernel  ## keep_effects = TRUE is required for $genetic_cor_env fit <- kernel_model(y = "value", env = "env", gid = "gid",                     data = maizeYield, random = K,                     keep_effects = TRUE)  megaenv <- cluster_environments(fit) megaenv$table #>   env cluster sil_width #> 1  IP       1    1.0000 #> 2  NM       2    1.0000 #> 4  SE       3    0.9580 #> 3  PM       3    0.9566 #> 5  SO       4    1.0000  ## 5. Feed the clusters into a cluster-aware model fit_cl <- kernel_model_clustered(y = "value", data = maizeYield,                                  random = K, env = "env", gid = "gid",                                  clusters = megaenv, use = "block") # }

Low power; treat as hypothesis-generating. #>   column  PC          r          p      p.adj n #> 1     y1 PC2 -0.9252402 0.02426079 0.09704317 5 #> 2     y1 PC4 -0.3163203 0.60406959 0.83213929 5 #> 3     y1 PC3 -0.1624467 0.79407975 0.83213929 5 #> 4     y1 PC1  0.1322238 0.83213929 0.83213929 5 # }  # \donttest{ ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------- ## WORKED EXAMPLE: marker effect networks -> eigenmarkers -> environmental PCs ## ## The full analysis chain of Della Coletta et al. (2023), on simulated data ## where the answer is known in advance so the method can be checked. ## ## Planted truth: ##   module A markers respond to mid-season TEMPERATURE ##   module B markers respond to late-season PRECIPITATION ##   module C markers have real but environment-INDEPENDENT effects ## ----------------------------------------------------------------------  ## --- 0. Simulate markers, weather and phenotypes --------------------- set.seed(2026) n.gid <- 160 n.marker <- 90 n.env <- 20 envs <- paste0("E", seq_len(n.env)) drivers <- scale(matrix(rnorm(n.env * 2), n.env, 2)) rownames(drivers) <- envs M <- scale(matrix(rbinom(n.gid * n.marker, 2, 0.5), n.gid, n.marker)) dimnames(M) <- list(paste0("G", seq_len(n.gid)),                     paste0("m", seq_len(n.marker))) beta <- matrix(0.2, n.marker, n.env) beta[1:30, ] <- rep(0.2 + 0.3 * drivers[, 1], each = 30) beta[31:60, ] <- rep(0.2 + 0.3 * drivers[, 2], each = 30) signal <- M %*% beta Y <- signal + matrix(rnorm(length(signal), sd = 0.3), n.gid, n.env) dimnames(Y) <- list(rownames(M), envs)  wth <- expand.grid(daysFromStart = 1:151, env = envs) ie <- match(wth$env, envs) day <- wth$daysFromStart wth$T2M <- 22 + 4 * sin(pi * day / 151) +   3 * drivers[ie, 1] * (day >= 50 & day <= 100) +   rnorm(nrow(wth), sd = 0.5) wth$PRECTOT <- exp(1 + 0.6 * drivers[ie, 2] * (day >= 100) +                      rnorm(nrow(wth), sd = 0.1))  ## --- 1. Marker effects per environment (RR-BLUP) ---------------------- ## Solve via the n x n system: with p markers >> n genotypes this is far ## cheaper than the p x p form and gives the same ridge solution. rrblup_effects <- function(y, Z, h2 = 0.5) {   yc <- as.numeric(y) - mean(y)   lambda <- ncol(Z) * (1 - h2) / h2   a <- solve(tcrossprod(Z) + lambda * diag(nrow(Z)), yc)   as.numeric(crossprod(Z, a)) } beta.hat <- sapply(colnames(Y), function(e) rrblup_effects(Y[, e], M, h2 = 0.55)) dimnames(beta.hat) <- list(colnames(M), colnames(Y))  ## --- 2. Marker effect network -> modules ------------------------------ ## Markers whose effects do not VARY across environments cannot covary with ## anything; screening them out first avoids NA correlations and spurious ## modules. The paper used WGCNA; this is the same idea in base R. eff.sd <- apply(beta.hat, 1, sd) Bk     <- beta.hat[eff.sd > quantile(eff.sd, 0.35), , drop = FALSE] adj    <- abs(cor(t(Bk)))^6                 # soft-thresholding power mods   <- cutree(hclust(as.dist(1 - adj), method = "average"), h = 0.92) mods   <- mods[mods %in% as.integer(names(table(mods))[table(mods) >= 15])]  ## --- 3. Eigenmarkers -------------------------------------------------- ## PC1 of a module's effect profiles, the analogue of a WGCNA module ## eigengene. Sign is arbitrary in PCA, so orient it deterministically -- ## otherwise a module can flip between runs and reverse every downstream ## correlation. eigenmarker <- function(B.mod) {   X  <- scale(t(B.mod))   em <- prcomp(X, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)$x[, 1]   if (mean(cor(em, X)) < 0) em <- -em   em } ids <- sort(unique(mods)) EM  <- sapply(ids, function(m) eigenmarker(Bk[names(mods)[mods == m], , drop = FALSE])) dimnames(EM) <- list(colnames(beta.hat), paste0("ME", ids))  ## --- 4. Environmental PCA and association ----------------------------- W  <- env_indices(wth, interval = 3, end.day = 151,                   statistic.by = c(PRECTOT = "sum")) #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> env_indices -- builds interval-resolved environmental indices #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> ------------------------------------------------------------ #> env_indices(): 20 environments x 2 factors x 51 intervals = 102 indices #>   interval width : 3 day(s), days 1..151 #> ------------------------------------------------------------ pc <- env_pca(W) #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> env_pca -- runs PCA on the environmental index matrix #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> ------------------------------------------------------------ #> env_pca(): 20 environments x 102 indices #>   informative PCs: 19 (= n.env - 1) #>   PC1 25.7%, PC2 16.4%, cumulative 42.1% #> ------------------------------------------------------------ assoc <- env_pc_associate(pc, EM, n.pc = 9, p.adjust = "BH") #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> env_pc_associate -- correlates PCs with an external variable #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> Strongest: ME1 ~ PC1, r = -0.77, p = 7.77e-05, FDR p = 0.0014 (n = 20) head(assoc) #>   column  PC           r            p       p.adj  n #> 1    ME1 PC1 -0.76768107 0.0000776952 0.001398514 20 #> 2    ME2 PC1  0.73762697 0.0002058673 0.001852806 20 #> 3    ME1 PC2 -0.62673494 0.0031054106 0.018632464 20 #> 4    ME2 PC2 -0.60348651 0.0048437536 0.021796891 20 #> 5    ME2 PC4 -0.12352845 0.6038587012 0.982526789 20 #> 6    ME2 PC5 -0.09614311 0.6867892239 0.982526789 20  ## --- 5. Name the drivers of an associated PC (paper Fig. 6c) ---------- k <- as.integer(sub("PC", "", assoc$PC[1])) L <- data.frame(factor = pc$meta$factor, day = pc$meta$day,                 loading = pc$loadings[, k]) sort(tapply(abs(L$loading), L$factor, mean), decreasing = TRUE) #>        T2M    PRECTOT  #> 0.08056294 0.07779317  env_loading_curve(pc, pc = k) #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> env_loading_curve -- plots seasonal PC loading curves #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> ---------------------------------------------------------------   ## --- 6. Permutation null, and why it is NOT enough -------------------- ## Permuting environment labels of the eigenmarker breaks the ## environment<->module link while preserving both structures. perm.max <- replicate(500, {   EMp <- EM[sample(nrow(EM)), , drop = FALSE]   rownames(EMp) <- rownames(EM)   max(abs(env_pc_associate(pc, EMp, n.pc = 9, verbose = FALSE)$r)) }) quantile(perm.max, 0.95)   # compare observed |r| with the permutation null #>       95%  #> 0.6557894   ## A spurious module can pass both FDR adjustment and this permutation test. ## The permutation preserves the module definitions, so it cannot detect a ## module that was spuriously assembled in the first place. Guard against ## this with module stability across resampled genotypes, or by requiring ## an independent set of environments -- not with permutation alone. # }

Return period simply 1 / freq inherits usual caveats: average recurrence interval estimated finite record, schedule. 20 years data return period ~10 seasons barely distinguishable noise. function print return period longer record. title: Retrieve FAO GAEZ Agro-Ecological Zone Classification for Sites — get_AEZ
text: env.id character vector. Environment/site identifiers. lat numeric vector. Latitude decimal degrees (WGS84), length env.id. lon numeric vector. Longitude decimal degrees (WGS84), length env.id. file character. Path GAEZ GeoTIFF already disk. NULL (default), get_AEZ uses raster shipped package (system.file("extdata", "aez_v9v2red_5m_CRUTS32_Hist_8110_100_avg.tif", package = "EnvRtype")). bundled file unavailable fall back downloading url. Supply file use different GAEZ release scenario. url character. Download URL GAEZ raster, used file NULL bundled raster missing. Defaults aez_default_url(), best-effort template verified live FAO server – see Details. dir.path character. cache downloaded raster. Default tempdir(). Use persistent directory avoid re-downloading. legend data.frame NULL. Lookup table least code label columns. NULL (default) uses aez_legend(). Pass NA skip labelling return raw codes . buffer numeric. greater 0, radius metres circular neighbourhood summarised around point (majority class share), rather single-cell lookup. Default 0. overwrite boolean. Re-download even cached file exists. Default FALSE. timeout integer. Seconds allowed download. Default 1800; GAEZ rasters large R's 60-second default abort . verbose boolean. Progress messages. Default TRUE.

title: Retrieve FAO GAEZ Agro-Ecological Zone Classification for Sites — get_AEZ
text: data.frame one row per environment: env environment id lat, lon coordinates supplied aez_code raster cell value aez_label, thermal, moisture, arable legend, one used majority_share buffer > 0, proportion cells     neighbourhood holding majority class – purity measure raster path used attached "source" attribute.

title: Retrieve FAO GAEZ Agro-Ecological Zone Classification for Sites — get_AEZ
text: raster comes . GAEZ v4 documented per-point API: publishes whole-globe GeoTIFFs JavaScript portal. get_AEZ therefore raster-extract tool resolves raster three steps – explicit file, else layer bundled inst/extdata, else download url. bundled layer GAEZ v4 57-class AEZ historical baseline (CRUTS32_Hist_8110, ~5 arc-min), makes default call fully offline reproducible. default URL unverified. used file bundled raster unavailable. FAO reorganised GAEZ download paths releases portal JavaScript-rendered, stable path confirmed. download triggered fails: open https://gaez.fao.org/pages/data-access-download, download AEZ classification layer manually, pass file file = "path//layer.tif". Coordinates must WGS84 lon/lat. reprojected raster's CRS automatically, raster declares one. raster undefined CRS triggers error rather silent mis-extraction. Interpreting buffer. single-cell lookup ~9 km resolution can misleading near zone boundary. buffer > 0 returned majority_share shows homogeneous neighbourhood ; value near 1 means site sits well inside one zone, 0.4 means classification effectively arbitrary location.

what: Envirotype-informed Kernels for Multi-Environment Genomic Prediction — get_kernel
title: Envirotype-informed Kernels for Multi-Environment Genomic Prediction — get_kernel
text: Builds genomic, envirotypic genotype--environment kernels required kernel_model. Given genomic relationship matrix (p x p genotypes) optionally environmental relationship matrix (q x q environments), returns one kernel per model term, already spectrally decomposed ready sample . Two computational engines available produce numerically identical results: engine = "factored" (default) Never allocates     n x n kernel. kernel represented eigenvectors     U (n x r) eigenvalues s, obtained small     p x p / q x q inputs. Memory O(n*r) instead O(n^2),     makes large multi-environment trials feasible. engine = "dense" Builds explicit n x n matrix     attaches $Kernel. Slower quadratic memory, needed     want inspect post-process kernel . Set verbose = TRUE trace step timings; verbose = FALSE (default) entirely silent.

title: Envirotype-informed Kernels for Multi-Environment Genomic Prediction — get_kernel

NULL, benchmark genomic-models built model restricted MM / MDs. data data.frame environment, genotype phenotype columns. model character. One "MM", "MDs", "EMM", "EMDs", "RNMM", "RNMDs". See Model structures. intercept.random logical. Append identity genotype kernel KG_Gi, separating marker-predictable genetic variance genotype-specific deviation markers capture. Requires replication (genotype seen one environment) identifiable; one observation per genotype confounded residual warning issued. Default FALSE. engine character. "factored" (default) "dense". env, gid, y character. Column names data. tol numeric. Eigenvalue cutoff, relative largest eigenvalue. Must match kernel_model(tol =). Default 1e-10. keep_var numeric (0, 1]. Retain leading eigenvalues carrying proportion kernel's trace. Sampler cost scales total rank, e.g. 0.99 often large speedup negligible change predictions. Default 1 (keep everything). scale_kernels logical. Normalise kernel mean(diag(K)) = 1 decomposing. Must match kernel_model(scale_kernels =). Default TRUE. verbose logical. Narrate step timings. Default FALSE.

what: Why the factored engine is exact
title: Envirotype-informed Kernels for Multi-Environment Genomic Prediction — get_kernel
text: Every kernel congruence transform small matrix. ig mapping observations genotypes ie environments, $$K_G = Z_g K_g Z_g' = K_g[ig, ig], \quad K_E = K_e[ie, ie]$$ eigendecomposition n x n kernel follows small one O(p^3) rather O(n^3). Writing \(K = '\) \(= V[ig,]\sqrt{D}\), nonzero eigenpairs come small Gram matrix \('\), giving orthonormal U exact eigenvalues. interaction kernel elementwise product two expansions, expansion Kronecker product: \(j = (ie-1) n_g + ig\), \(K_{GE} = (K_e \otimes K_g)[j, j]\). complete balanced grid eigenpairs closed-form (eigenvalues \(d_e \otimes d_g\), eigenvectors Khatri-Rao product) large eigendecomposition ever required.

Rewriting one state file every iteration risk whole file kill mid-write; appending risks last line, reader tolerates truncated final record. fingerprint. manifest stores hash coordinates, dates variables. Resuming different arguments refused, silently concatenating two different queries produces table looks fine means nothing. Failures abort run. failed environment logged loop continues. title: Kernel Models for Predicting Phenotypes across Multi-Environment Conditions — kernel_model
text: Fits Bayesian linear mixed models multi-environment trials (MET) using kernels produced get_kernel(). model $$y = 1\mu + X\beta + \sum_j u_j + e$$ \(u_j \sim N(0, K_j \sigma^2_j)\) \(e \sim N(0, \sigma^2_e)\). Sampling runs spectral basis kernel, every kernel used eigendecomposition rather n x n matrix. function returns genotype predictions, per-kernel variance components, broad- narrow-sense heritabilities, – keep_effects = TRUE – posterior effect chains breeder-facing report tables (per-environment rankings, stability, selection candidates). Set verbose = TRUE trace six execution steps per-step total timings; verbose = FALSE (default) entirely silent.

Writing \(K_j = U_j S_j U_j'\), effects sampled \(u_j = U_j b_j\) \(b_j \sim N(0, S_j \sigma^2_{u_j})\), cost per iteration scales retained rank kernel, \(n^2\). title: Kernel Models for Predicting Phenotypes across Multi-Environment Conditions — kernel_model
text: Two defects original parameterisation addressed arguments: R2_split. original gave every kernel full R2 share, nk kernels priors collectively assert nk * R2 phenotypic variance – RNMDs (4 kernels, R2 = 0.5) twice var(y). "per_kernel" (default) uses R2 / nk total prior mass stays R2 regardless model size, keeping model comparisons equal footing. "shared" restores original behaviour. prior_scale. Kernels normalised mean(diag(K)) = 1 equal scale effective dimension: rank-5 rank-750 kernel mean diagonal carry different total variance. "eigen" (default) divides prior scale mean(s) (= trace / rank), making priors comparable across kernels differing rank.

title: Map scanned predictions, or training-network coverage — map_scan
text: Three kinds map available `type`: `"performance"`: predicted value (`yHat`) one     genotypes across scanned sites, one panel per genotype (single     panel mean `summarise = "mean"`). Sites outside training     covariate envelope drawn grey crosses rather value     scale. `"coverage"`: training network actually supports     prediction, colouring site geometric position relative     training covariate cloud (interpolation, edge, mild-     gross-extrapolation). `"which_won_where"`: classic -won-view     selection. answers two questions two maps (two tables).     won single top genotype per site, posterior     mean (`yHat`; ties broken first genotype). Winners     many genotypes statistically tied win, taken scan's     posterior draws: genotype co-winner probability     best site (`prob_win`) least `win_threshold`. count     (`n_winners`) tied genotypes (`winners`, probable first)     reported per site, can see decision clear (one     winner) versus several genotypes indistinguishable. needs     scan current [scan_untested_envs()], stores per-site     win probabilities.

title: Map scanned predictions, or training-network coverage — map_scan
code: ## A scan is normally produced by scan_untested_envs(); here we build a ## minimal one by hand -- 2 genotypes predicted at 9 sites on a 3x3 grid. sites <- paste0("S", 1:9) grid  <- expand.grid(lon = 1:3, lat = 1:3) yh <- rbind(G1 = 6 + grid$lon * 0.3 - grid$lat * 0.1,             G2 = 5 + grid$lat * 0.4) colnames(yh) <- sites scan <- list(   yHat_matrix = yh, yHat_lower = yh - 0.4, yHat_upper = yh + 0.4,   ## posterior P(best) per genotype x site (illustrative softmax of yHat)   yHat_prob_win = prop.table(exp(yh), margin = 2),   interpolation = data.frame(     env               = sites,     position          = rep(c("interpolation", "edge",                               "gross_extrapolation"), each = 3),     mahalanobis_ratio = seq(0.5, 3.5, length.out = 9),     prop_outside      = seq(0, 0.8, length.out = 9),     weight_negativity = 0, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)) class(scan) <- "scan_untested_envs"  ## Site coordinates, keyed by the scanned environment name coords <- data.frame(env = sites, lon = grid$lon, lat = grid$lat)  # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {   ## Where does the training network support prediction?   map_scan(scan, coords, type = "coverage")    ## Predicted performance for a single genotype   map_scan(scan, coords, type = "performance", genotypes = "G1")    ## Mean over several genotypes in one panel   map_scan(scan, coords, type = "performance",            genotypes = c("G1", "G2"), summarise = "mean")    ## Which genotype wins at each site, and how many genotypes tie it   ww <- map_scan(scan, coords, type = "which_won_where")   ww$who_won_where   ww$winners }  # }  ## Export the plotted data instead of a figure, to map it your own way head(map_scan(scan, coords, type = "coverage", output = "table")) #>   gid env lon lat yHat lower upper      position mahalanobis_ratio prop_outside #> 1  G1  S1   1   1  6.2   5.8   6.6 interpolation             0.500          0.0 #> 2  G1  S2   2   1  6.5   6.1   6.9 interpolation             0.875          0.1 #> 3  G1  S3   3   1  6.8   6.4   7.2 interpolation             1.250          0.2 #> 4  G1  S4   1   2  6.1   5.7   6.5          edge             1.625          0.3 #> 5  G1  S5   2   2  6.4   6.0   6.8          edge             2.000          0.4 #> 6  G1  S6   3   2  6.7   6.3   7.1          edge             2.375          0.5 #>   weight_negativity ci_width  prob_win flagged #> 1                 0      0.8 0.6899745   FALSE #> 2                 0      0.8 0.7502601   FALSE #> 3                 0      0.8 0.8021839   FALSE #> 4                 0      0.8 0.5744425   FALSE #> 5                 0      0.8 0.6456563   FALSE #> 6                 0      0.8 0.7109495   FALSE  ## Both winner tables (no ggplot2 needed), one row per site ww_tab <- map_scan(scan, coords, type = "which_won_where", output = "table") head(ww_tab$who_won_where) #>   env lon lat winner winner_yHat winner_prob      position flagged #> 1  S1   1   1     G1         6.2   0.6899745 interpolation   FALSE #> 2  S2   2   1     G1         6.5   0.7502601 interpolation   FALSE #> 3  S3   3   1     G1         6.8   0.8021839 interpolation   FALSE #> 4  S4   1   2     G1         6.1   0.5744425          edge   FALSE #> 5  S5   2   2     G1         6.4   0.6456563          edge   FALSE #> 6  S6   3   2     G1         6.7   0.7109495          edge   FALSE head(ww_tab$winners) #>   env lon lat n_winners winners  max_prob      position flagged #> 1  S1   1   1         2  G1, G2 0.6899745 interpolation   FALSE #> 2  S2   2   1         1      G1 0.7502601 interpolation   FALSE #> 3  S3   3   1         1      G1 0.8021839 interpolation   FALSE #> 4  S4   1   2         2  G1, G2 0.5744425          edge   FALSE #> 5  S5   2   2         2  G1, G2 0.6456563          edge   FALSE #> 6  S6   3   2         2  G1, G2 0.7109495          edge   FALSE  # \donttest{ ## ---- Realistic scan: 50 new locations across Mato Grosso, Brazil -------- ## The bundled maize datasets are multi-environment trials from Mato Grosso: ## maizeWTH (daily weather), maizeYield (grain yield) and maizeG (genomic ## relationships). We train on them, then predict the trained genotypes at ## 50 candidate sites spread across the state. Needs BGGE (fitting) and a ## network connection (get_weather() queries NASA POWER). data("maizeWTH"); data("maizeYield"); data("maizeG")  ## 1. Training environmental covariates (first 100 days after sowing) vars <- c("FRUE", "PETP", "GDD", "T2M_MAX") Wtr  <- W_matrix(env.data = maizeWTH[maizeWTH$daysFromStart < 100, ],                  var.id = vars, statistic = "mean") #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> W_matrix -- builds the environmental covariable (W) matrix #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #>   - summarising weather data into environmental covariables #>   - centring, scaling and quality-controlling W  ## 2. Kernels + a fit that KEEPS the effect chains (required by any scan) K   <- get_kernel(K_G = list(G = maizeG),                   K_E = list(W = env_kernel(env.data = Wtr)[[2]]),                   data = maizeYield, model = "RNMM",                   env = "env", gid = "gid", y = "value") #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> env_kernel -- builds environmental relatedness kernels #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #>   - computing a single environmental kernel fit <- kernel_model(y = "value", data = maizeYield, random = K,                     env = "env", gid = "gid",                     iterations = 5000, burnin = 1000, keep_effects = TRUE)  ## 3. Fifty candidate locations across Mato Grosso (WGS84 decimal degrees). ##    The state spans roughly 7.3-18.0 S and 50.2-61.6 W. set.seed(2024) coords <- data.frame(   env = sprintf("MT%02d", 1:50),   lon = runif(50, -61.6, -50.2),   lat = runif(50, -18.0,  -7.3))  ## 4. Daily weather for each site over one summer season, processed into the ##    SAME covariates as the training matrix. wth_new <- get_weather(env.id = coords$env, lat = coords$lat, lon = coords$lon,                        start.day = "2023-11-01", end.day = "2024-02-15",                        variables.names = c("T2M", "T2M_MAX", "T2M_MIN",                                            "T2MDEW", "PRECTOT", "RH2M",                                            "ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN")) #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> get_weather -- downloads daily weather from NASA POWER #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> get_weather() - daily weather from NASA POWER #> https://docs.ropensci.org/nasapower #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> Start .............................. Thu Oct 22 18:34:44 2026 #> Total time ......................... 27.64s wth_new <- processWTH(wth_new)          # derives FRUE, PETP, GDD, ... #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> processWTH -- derives all agro-meteorological parameters #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> Dropping existing column(s) before recomputation: N, RTA, VPD #>   - radiation parameters computed #>   - atmospheric-demand parameters computed #>   - temperature-response parameters computed Wnew <- W_matrix(env.data = wth_new[wth_new$daysFromStart < 100, ],                  var.id = vars, statistic = "mean") #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #> W_matrix -- builds the environmental covariable (W) matrix #> Last updated at 09/27/2026 #> --------------------------------------------------------------- #>   - summarising weather data into environmental covariables #>   - centring, scaling and quality-controlling W  ## 5. title: Predict Trained Genotypes at Untested Environments Without Refitting — scan_untested_envs
text: Transfers fitted kernel_model environments never planted – new locations, new planting dates, – using environmental covariates. re-fitting phenotypes new sites required. environmental main effect estimated training sites kriged onto new site linear environmental kernel, whole posterior carried draw--draw credible intervals, win probabilities extrapolation diagnostic internally consistent. transfer. Covariates standardised training moments, $$\tilde{W} = (W - \bar{W}_{tr}) \; / \; s_{tr},$$ linear (product) environmental kernel formed \(p\) covariates, $$K_{tt} = \tilde{W}_{tr}\tilde{W}_{tr}^{\top}/p, \quad       K_{nt} = \tilde{W}_{n}\tilde{W}_{tr}^{\top}/p, \quad       K_{nn} = \tilde{W}_{n}\tilde{W}_{n}^{\top}/p.$$ new-site environmental effects kriging (Gaussian-process conditional-mean) map training effects, $$H = K_{nt}\,(K_{tt} + \lambda )^{-1}, \qquad       \hat{e}_{n}^{(d)} = H\,e_{tr}^{(d)},$$ applied every retained MCMC draw \(d\). GxE kernel present interaction effects kriged way. ridge \(\lambda\) stabilises inverse; \(H\) constrained positive, large negative row weights signal site reached extrapolation (see weight_negativity ). prediction. draw \(d\), genotype \(g\) new site \(j\), $$\hat{y}^{(d)}_{gj} = \mu + u_g^{(d)} + \hat{e}^{(d)}_{j}        + \widehat{(ge)}^{(d)}_{gj},$$ \(\mu\) training grand mean. Point predictions posterior means draws credible interval uses empirical quantiles \(\alpha=(1-\texttt{level})/2\) \(1-\alpha\). probability genotype best site fraction draws attains row maximum, respects genotype correlation within draw. Per-site genomic heritability reported \(h^2 = \sigma^2_g / (\sigma^2_g + \sigma^2_e)\).

Several complementary measures returned single one sufficient: Cosine similarity nearest training site,     \(s_{ij} = K_{nt,ij}/\sqrt{K_{nn,ii}\,K_{tt,jj}}\), summarised     max_similarity mean_similarity. Mahalanobis-type distance leading principal-component     subspace (enough PCs reach 95% variance),     \(d_i = \sqrt{\sum_k z_{ik}^2}\), divided 95th percentile     training distances give mahalanobis_ratio. marginal range test per covariate (prop_outside,     max_exceedance_sd). marginal: site inside every     covariate's range individually can still occupy combination     never occurred, distance weight measures catch. Kriging-weight geometry: weight_negativity     \(= \sum_j \min(H_{ij},0)\) effective number training sites     leaned , \(n_{\mathrm{eff},} = (\sum_j |H_{ij}|)^2 / \sum_j H_{ij}^2\). combined divergence_index     \(= \min\!\big(1, \max(0,\; 0.5(1-s_{\max}) + 0.5\,t)\big)\)     \(t = \mathrm{clamp}((\texttt{mahalanobis\_ratio}-0.5)/2,\,0,\,1)\). Sites labelled "interpolation", "edge", "mild_extrapolation" "gross_extrapolation" . Position geometry, correctness guarantee. Calibration 60 held-environments found envelope measures correlate \(r \approx -0.37\) \(-0.66\) realised accuracy. Treat position label description site lies, never verdict prediction right wrong. model-internal ci_width_ratio strongest single accuracy correlate (\(r=-0.66\)); know true accuracy, run leave-environments-cross-validation data.

title: Simulate an Envirome with a Known Relationship to an Environment Correlation — sim_W
text: Construction. \(C_{env}^{1/2}\) symmetric PSD square root target, orthonormal driver \(O\) (\(q\times n_{var}\)) iid noise \(E\), $$W = \sqrt{1-}\; C_{env}^{1/2} O \; + \; \sqrt{}\; E,$$ environmental kernel follows env_kernel convention $$K_W = \frac{W W^{\top}}{\mathrm{tr}(W W^{\top})/q}.$$ Recovery measured -diagonal Pearson correlation \(r = \mathrm{cor}\big(\mathrm{offdiag}(K_W),\, \mathrm{offdiag}(C_{env})\big)\). Calibration. calibrate = TRUE, noise outcome scale: internal variance share \(\) solved uniroot \(E[r] = 1 - \mathrm{noise}\). \(r\) decreases \(\), noise = 0 gives \(= 0\) (full recovery) noise = 1 gives \(= 1\) (pure noise). Collinearity. collinearity > 0, share columns collapsed onto n_blocks driver families, mimicking redundancy real enviromes lowering effective rank. C_env environment correlation, kinship. must \(q\times q\) unit diagonal. Passing genomic kinship rejected. Realism knobs. marginal maps covariable non-Gaussian shape (rank-preserving), kernel = "rbf" builds Gaussian instead linear kernel, family.sizes groups columns named covariable families (real enviromes), na.frac injects missing values returned \(W\) truth computed, downstream cleaning (e.g. W_matrix imputation) can tested known answer.

text: environment gets latent profile drives covariables; structure controls profiles arranged. "random" places environments independently (maximal diversity), "clusters" groups n_cluster mega-environments (high within-cluster similarity, -cluster similarity set .cor), "gradient" orders environments along latent continuum (neighbours similar, extremes different), latitude season gradient. redundancy collapses share covariables onto n_blocks drivers, lowering effective rank, marginal reshapes covariables away Gaussian.

title: Simulate a Marker Matrix with a Controllable Genetic Diversity — sim_markers
text: Allele frequencies drawn per marker genotypes \(x_{ij}\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(2, p_{j})\). Population structure follows Balding–Nichols model: within subpopulation \(s\) frequency drifts ancestral \(p_j\) \(p_{sj}\sim\mathrm{Beta}\!\big(p_j\tfrac{1-F_{ST}}{F_{ST}}, (1-p_j)\tfrac{1-F_{ST}}{F_{ST}}\big)\), larger \(F_{ST}\) means -group differentiation lower within-group diversity. Linkage disequilibrium emulated copying block's lead marker fraction ld markers block, lowering effective rank kinship.

C_env target environment correlation, realised     correlation attached attribute "realised". truth list everything known: genetic values g,     target/realised correlations, target/realised heritabilities     bases, variances, means. title: Simulate a Multi-Environment Trial with a Known Genetic Architecture — sim_met
text: Model. \(n\) lines \(q\) environments, genetic values drawn separable (Kronecker) Gaussian $$\mathrm{vec}(G) \sim \mathcal{N}\!\left(0,\; K \otimes \Sigma_g\right),       \qquad \Sigma_g = D^{1/2}\, C\, D^{1/2},\; D = \mathrm{diag}(\sigma^2_g),$$ realised \(G = L_K\, U\, L_C^{\top}\) \(L_K L_K^{\top}=K\), \(L_C L_C^{\top}=\Sigma_g\). exact = TRUE driver \(U\) orthonormalised \(U^{\top}U = nI\), making realised moments match targets instead merely scattering around . Phenotypes. replicate \(r\), $$y_{ijr} = \mu_j + g_{ij} + \varepsilon_{ijr}, \qquad       \varepsilon_{ijr}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2_{e,j}),\quad       \sigma^2_{e,j} = \sigma^2_{g,j}\,\frac{1-h^2_j}{h^2_j}.$$ Heritability, two bases. plot-basis value \(h^2 = V_g/(V_g+V_e)\) min.h2/max.h2 target; line-mean basis \(h^2/(h^2 + (1-h^2)/n_{rep})\) also reported. Realised environment correlation measured K-whitened scale. lines related \(K\), cor(G) across lines \(C\); forcing wrong. realised correlation defined \(\mathrm{cor}(L_K^{-1} G)\) stored validation. two matrices different objects. K \(n\times n\) among lines; environment correlation \(q\times q\). genomic kinship passed environment correlation expected common error rejected elementwise unit-diagonal check. Alternative genetic mechanisms. Besides default separable draw, three opt-mechanisms generate genetic values: Reaction norm (supply W): genetic values built     causally envirome, \(g_{ij} = m_i + \sum_k w_{jk} b_{ik}\)     main effect \(m\) line sensitivities \(b_{\cdot k}\)     \(K\)-structured. environment correlation induced     W (reported), imposed. rn.main splits variance     main effect reaction-norm interaction. Marker-based (supply markers): QTL effects sampled per     environment target correlation C, giving large-effect     architectures instead infinitesimal draw. Multiple kinships (supply list K     K.weights): independent additive, dominance epistatic components     summed. gxe.specific adds line-independent, environment-specific deviation makes covariance non-separable. rep.var spatial (AR1\(\times\)AR1 field) add trial realism phenotypes.

Sample the ## area of interest, here 40 points around each of 5 locations. sites <- data.frame(   env = c("SOR", "LON", "SLG", "PAL", "BAR"),   lat = c(-12.5453, -23.3045, -28.4083, -10.1689, -12.1530),   lon = c(-55.7113, -51.1696, -54.9608, -48.3317, -44.9900))  g <- expand.grid(k = 1:40, i = seq_len(nrow(sites))) pts <- data.frame(   env  = paste0(sites$env[g$i], "_", sprintf("%03d", g$k)),   farm = sites$env[g$i],   lat  = sites$lat[g$i] + runif(nrow(g), -0.05, 0.05),   lon  = sites$lon[g$i] + runif(nrow(g), -0.05, 0.05))  soil_grid <- get_soil(env.id = pts$env, lat = pts$lat, lon = pts$lon,                       variables.names = c("clay", "sand", "silt",                                           "soc", "phh2o"))  fit <- soil_classification(soil_grid,                            variables = c("clay", "sand", "silt",                                          "soc", "phh2o"),                            depths    = c("0_5cm", "30_60cm"),                            risk.vars = "soc") fit  ## Do farms split across zones? Usually the interesting question. table(farm = pts$farm, cluster = fit$classification$cluster)   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 3. Posterior probabilities and ambiguous sites ## --------------------------------------------------------------- round(head(fit$posterior), 3)        # membership in EVERY zone  ## Sites the model is least sure about -- these sit on a boundary. amb <- fit$classification[fit$classification$uncertain, ] amb[order(amb$max_posterior), ]  ## Tighten or relax the flag without refitting the model: fit2 <- soil_classification(soil_grid, uncertainty.threshold = 0.9) sum(fit2$classification$uncertain)   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 4. Ordering zones so cluster 1 always means the same thing ## --------------------------------------------------------------- lo  <- soil_classification(soil_grid, risk.vars = "soc",                            risk.direction = "high")   # 1 = lowest SOC hi  <- soil_classification(soil_grid, risk.vars = "soc",                            risk.direction = "low")    # 1 = highest SOC lo$profiles[, c("cluster", "n_sites")]   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 5. Many correlated variables: reduce first ## --------------------------------------------------------------- fit_pca <- soil_classification(soil_grid, use.pca = TRUE, pca.var = 0.95) fit_pca$pca                          # how many components were kept  ## Or restrict the covariance family when sites are few: fit_par <- soil_classification(soil_grid, model.names = c("EII", "VII",                                                           "EEI", "VVI"))   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 6. Joining results back to your own table ## --------------------------------------------------------------- out <- merge(pts, fit$classification, by = "env") head(out[, c("env", "farm", "lat", "lon", "cluster",              "max_posterior", "uncertain")])  ## Dominant zone per farm, and whether the farm is homogeneous with(out, table(farm, cluster))   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 7. Is the cluster count actually supported? ## --------------------------------------------------------------- fit$BIC                              # full table over G and family fit$model$G                          # selected number of zones ## print(fit) reports the gap to the runner-up; a weak gap (< 2) means ## the zone count is not settled, whatever the point estimate says. } # }

title: Daily Soil Water Balance and Crop Water-Stress Indices — water_balance
text: Method. FAO-56 single crop coefficient approach (Allen et al. 1998, Ch. 8). Root-zone depletion stepped forward daily: $$D_{r,} = D_{r,-1} - P_i - I_i + ET_{,} + DP_i$$ bounded \([0, TAW]\). Water excess field capacity becomes deep percolation; depletion exceed total available water. stress coefficient follows FAO-56 Eq. 84: $$K_s = 1 \quad \mathrm{}\ D_r \le RAW$$ $$K_s = \frac{TAW - D_r}{TAW - RAW} \quad \mathrm{}\ D_r > RAW$$ transpiration proceeds potential rate readily available water exhausted, declines linearly zero wilting point. Causal ordering. Ks day \(\) computed yesterday's depletion today's capacity. Using day's closing depletion let today's rainfall relieve stress already reduced today's transpiration – subtle look-ahead systematically understates stress. Units. SoilGrids serves integers mapped units: wv0033 = 314 means 0.314 cm3/cm3. Conversion automatic; see convert.units. Total available water integrated across SoilGrids layers intersecting root zone, weighted depth contributes, taken single layer. rooting depth grows season, TAW recomputed daily (cached unique depth speed). model. dual crop coefficient, soil evaporation separated transpiration. capillary rise, lateral flow, surface runoff – rainfall assumed infiltrate, overestimates stored water understates stress steep, crusted low-infiltration soils. Subtract runoff precipitation column beforehand matters. Irrigation applied given; balance schedule . Interpreting output. Regress Ks yield: bounded, dimensionless, scales transpiration directly. depletion_frac easier explain agronomists. stress_level convenience grouping tabulation used modelling covariate – discards magnitude.

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Requires live NASA POWER and SoilGrids services. ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 1. Minimal use ## --------------------------------------------------------------- wth  <- get_weather(env.id = "NM", lat = -13.05, lon = -56.05,                     start.day = "2015-02-15", end.day = "2015-06-15") wth  <- processWTH(wth)                 # adds ETP soil <- get_soil(env.id = "NM", lat = -13.05, lon = -56.05,                  variables.names = c("wv0033", "wv1500", "clay"))  wb <- water_balance(wth, soil) head(wb[, c("env", "daysFromStart", "TAW", "Dr", "Ks",             "deficit", "stress_level")])   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 2. Several environments at once ## --------------------------------------------------------------- sites <- data.frame(   env = c("SOR", "LON", "BAR"),   lat = c(-12.5453, -23.3045, -12.1530),   lon = c(-55.7113, -51.1696, -44.9900))  wth  <- processWTH(get_weather(env.id = sites$env, lat = sites$lat,                                lon = sites$lon,                                start.day = "2023-10-15",                                end.day   = "2024-02-12")) soil <- get_soil(env.id = sites$env, lat = sites$lat, lon = sites$lon,                  variables.names = c("wv0033", "wv1500"))  wb <- water_balance(wth, soil, root.depth = 1000) summary_water_balance(wb)   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 3. Irrigation: constant, per-day, or from a column ## --------------------------------------------------------------- water_balance(wth, soil, irrigation = 5)              # 5 mm every day water_balance(wth, soil, irrigation = rep(0, nrow(wth)))  wth$irr <- ifelse(wth$daysFromStart %in% 40:70, 8, 0)  # top-up at flowering wb_irr  <- water_balance(wth, soil, irrigation = "irr")  ## How much stress did irrigation remove? c(rainfed   = sum(water_balance(wth, soil, verbose = FALSE)$deficit),   irrigated = sum(wb_irr$deficit))   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 4. A different crop: soybean ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## Kc and p come from FAO-56 Tables 12 and 22. Always check them ## against your own crop, cycle length and region. wb_soy <- water_balance(   wth, soil,   kc.stages = c(1, 25, 50, 95, 120),   kc.values = c(0.40, 0.80, 1.15, 1.15, 0.50),   p         = 0.50,          # soybean, FAO-56 Table 22   root.depth = 800)   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 5. Restricted root zone (compaction, shallow profile) ## --------------------------------------------------------------- shallow <- water_balance(wth, soil, root.depth = 400, verbose = FALSE) deep    <- water_balance(wth, soil, root.depth = 1200, verbose = FALSE) c(shallow_TAW = max(shallow$TAW), deep_TAW = max(deep$TAW)) ## A shallower profile stores less water and stresses sooner.   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 6. Dry planting: start part-depleted rather than at field capacity ## --------------------------------------------------------------- wb_dry <- water_balance(wth, soil, initial.depletion = 60)   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 7. Season and growth-stage summaries ## --------------------------------------------------------------- summary_water_balance(wb)  summary_water_balance(wb, by.interval = TRUE,                       time.window  = c(0, 14, 35, 60, 90, 120),                       names.window = c("P-E", "E-V1", "V1-V4",                                        "V4-VT", "VT-GF", "GF-PM")) ## Stress at VT-GF (flowering to grain fill) costs far more yield ## than the same stress during vegetative growth.   ## --------------------------------------------------------------- ## 8. Using the indices as envirotype covariates ## --------------------------------------------------------------- W <- summary_water_balance(wb, by.interval = TRUE,                            time.window = c(0, 30, 60, 90, 120)) wide <- reshape(W[, c("env", "interval", "mean_Ks")],                 idvar = "env", timevar = "interval", direction = "wide") head(wide)   # one row per environment, ready to join to trial data } # }
